answer: Each identity claims one spiral chamber and locks a 70-credit bond, then files a kernel tone, a key-signed sequence tied to that chamber alone. An auditor replays the kernel tone; the chamber echo delay and decay must match the spiral geometry, or the bond burns. Filing costs 34 credits for the first identity and 34+8(k-1) for the kth, so the 1000th pays 8026 and 1,000 fakes pay 4,030,000 plus 70,000 locked. A rented-shell ring fails because one geometry yields one echo signature, so duplicate decays expose the ring. An honest agent pays 34 once and recovers the bond after a clean audit.
